author: Kylie Sczepanski
title: No long waits, delays at Lansing airport amid DHS shutdown - NewsBreak
text:
By Kylie Sczepanski ,
6 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — As the nation enters day 40 of a partial government shutdown, TSA workers are about to miss another paycheck—and many of them are calling out of work in droves.
That means at many major airports, lines for security are snaking through the building, with wait times hours longer than usual.
But here in Lansing, the Capitol Region International Airport is getting travelers through security in no time.
6 News spoke with some passengers at leaving their flight today said they had no issues with their travels — and lines for security are nonexistent.
It’s in stark contrast to the major airports across the country who are seeing wait times rising as TSA workers quit and call in sick en masse.
While spring break season is in full swing, a spokesperson with the airport says they are prepared for the expected influx of travelers. They say anyone worried about the larger airports still has time to switch their flight to leave from Lansing.
“It’s very easy to travel from Lansing and into Lansing,” said Narine Manukova, spokesperson for the airport. “We welcome all the travelers to look at the flights, we have plenty of nonstop destinations and if you’re traveling in the next two weeks you can still adjust your travel and fly from Lansing even if you do have to make connection once you pass security here at Lansing it’s a very easy experience.”
